## OQ-8 — RESOLVED 2026-08-27 by the owner: align with the documented contract

Surfaced by P2.127, which held the direction it was given (**never widen**) and then reported, honestly
and unprompted, that the direction contradicts upstream and two of our own siblings. That contradiction
is the question; the fix itself is done and the flip is **one branch**.

**What ships today (`1e2aa4438`):** an uncompilable `deny` or `ask` rule **still decides at its own
action**, over everything. Only a malformed `allow` is dropped, because dropping a grant narrows and
dropping a prohibition widens. So a Windows-style path in a deny list is an effective **deny-everything**
— fail-closed, and the user now gets a diagnostic naming the offending rule instead of a generic
"Permission DSL document is invalid", with the rest of the layer surviving.

**What contradicts it, all three measured by that lane:**

- `managed-settings.md#find-entries-claude-code-dropped` — an invalid permission rule is skipped
  **whatever its action** ("such as one invalid permission rule, with a warning for each"), and the same
  page argues against over-denying on an invalid deny value.
- Our own importer drops malformed deny rules.
- `managed-policy.ts:tolerantPermissionDsl` drops them too.

So the codebase now holds **three different answers** to one situation, and `AGENTS.md` states that
upstream docs are contracts.

**The case for keeping what shipped:** a rule that will not compile is a rule whose *intent is unknown*,
and guessing wrong in the permissive direction costs more than guessing wrong in the restrictive one.

**The case for aligning:** it is the documented contract, it removes a three-way inconsistency, and
keeping it has an inversion cost of exactly the shape P2.136 just fixed — the user wrote a **narrow**
deny and silently gets a **blanket** one, which is not what they asked for either.

Not blocking any other row. Whichever way it goes, `permission-dsl.test.ts` carries one now-half-stale
comment ("fails the layer closed" → fails the rule closed) whose assertion is green.

**RESOLVED 2026-08-27. The owner chose alignment: a permission rule that will not compile is dropped
whatever its action, with a warning for each.** `AGENTS.md` states upstream docs are contracts, the page
covers this exact case, and two of our own siblings already comply — so the shipped behaviour was the
odd one out of three, and a codebase holding three answers to one question is itself the defect.

**The contract is stronger than the question assumed, in the same direction.** The sentence quoted above
is from the managed-settings side; the executing lane found one covering **our actual surface** —
`managed-settings.md#keys-that-fail-closed`: *"User, project, and local settings files remain strict: …
an individual entry that fails, such as a malformed permission rule, is skipped with a warning while the
rest of the file applies."* That is this exact case, named, for user/project/local files.

**The accepted cost is WORSE than stated when this was decided, and the owner should know.** The ruling
was taken on the understanding that "a typo in a `deny` rule now stops denying, and a warning they may
not read is the only signal." Measured by the executing lane: **`CompiledPermissionDslV1.diagnostics`
has no consumer at all** — the sole production caller never reads it and no other reader exists. So it
is not that the user may miss the warning; **there is currently no warning to read.** The loss is
silent. This is pre-existing (P2.127 had the same gap) and is not a reason to reverse the ruling — the
contract says "with a warning", so wiring the warning is what makes us *comply*, not what softens the
decision. → P2.271, and it is the row that completes this one.
That is a real loss, and it is the price of the contract — the countervailing loss under the other
option was a narrow deny silently becoming a blanket one, which is the same intent-inversion P2.136 was
opened for.

Execution note for whoever takes it: the flip is one branch (§5 item 4 of that lane's report), **but it
is not only one branch**. `evaluateClaudeHookIfFilter`'s documented fail-open is coupled to the
`invalid-policy` id through a one-rule allow program, so a plain drop would **silently stop hooks
running**. That coupling is already pinned by a test — keep it green, and treat a red there as the
coupling firing, not as a flaky test. → P2.270.


## What counts as done — the stopping rule (owner, 2026-08-27)

This plan does not end when the tracker empties. It cannot: **66% of all rows were born from
our own work** (their notes say "Found by", "raised by", "residue"), the row count has grown
42 → 357 in six days at a steady ~+50/day with no deceleration, and the rate is coupled to
**how much we look**, not to how much is wrong. A queue fed by its own execution has no
natural end.

**So the boundary is coverage of the documented contract, not the state of the queue.**
Owner's rule, and it is better than the "close the user-facing defects" alternative it
replaced for one concrete reason: a doc corpus is **enumerable and external**, while
"user-facing enough" is a judgement that must be re-argued every time.

**Done means:** every page of the governing corpus has a verdict, and every gap those
verdicts produce is either closed or **explicitly deferred with a reason**. That is what the
coverage map and the P5.1 / P5.2 sweeps already are — they enumerate against the docs rather
than against our queue. The tracker is a work queue; it is not a completeness proof.

### Which corpus governs which runtime — and the asymmetry

| What we ship | Governing corpus | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `claude-runtime` | Claude docs (191 pages, `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`) | direct |
| **Pi** | **Claude docs as well** | **Pi is built TO Claude's documentation** — it has no separate contract of its own. So a Claude doc gap is a DOUBLE gap, and the Claude coverage map does duty for two runtimes. |
| `codex` | `developers.openai.com/plugins/` (3 useful pages) + `learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks.md` + practice in `github.com/openai/plugins` | spec and practice disagree; read both |
| **nestor remote agent** | **none** | It is a genuinely remote agent and no external corpus describes it. |

**Name the asymmetry rather than let it hide:** three of the four have an external document to
measure against; **the remote agent does not.** For it, "covered" cannot be measured — it has
to be *defined* by us, and that definition is owed. Until it exists, the stopping rule is
sound for three quarters of what we ship and silent about the rest, and a rule that is silent
somewhere will be read as satisfied there.

**A moving target, not a finish line.** The Claude corpus grows, and `AGENTS.md` records that
new pages are this fork's recurring failure mode — the count went 174 → 186 → 191 while the
guide still said 174. So "covered" is true against a snapshot, and the snapshot's date is part
of the claim.

### What this rule releases

Work with no governing page and no cross-runtime consequence — test hygiene, tooling traps,
doc-anchor rot, build ergonomics — is **normal maintenance and does not gate this plan**.
Roughly a third of the open rows are that class. They stay in the tracker as a record; they do
not hold the close-out. Judge them per row at close-out, not by the keyword sweep that
produced that third — that sweep was measured wrong once already, in the inverted direction.

### The tag that makes this answerable

Every row born from here on starts its note with one tag, written by whoever found it, at the
moment the cause is in front of them — **not inferred later by grep**, which has already
produced an almost exactly inverted answer once:

- `[doc:claude]` — a Claude page governs it (so it bears on **both** claude-runtime and Pi)
- `[doc:codex]` — a Codex page governs it
- `[doc:none]` — our own implementation; no upstream page decides the behaviour
- `[remote]` — specific to the nestor remote agent

Multiple tags are fine. Existing rows are **not** backfilled by guesswork; an open row gets
its tag when it is next dispatched, from the lane that measures it. Closed rows stay untagged,
which is harmless — the question this answers is about what remains.


## OQ-9 — OPEN: a benign, runnable PowerShell command is hard-denied

Surfaced by P2.287, which **verified** a review finding that had gone unchallenged twice, and
then correctly refused to act on it because acting reverses a security decision.

**Measured:** `Remove-Item -s ~ -Path ./logs` is runnable and benign. It removes a stream and
leaves the file; it touches nothing under home. Today it takes an **every-mode deny plus a
`nonNegotiable` prompt** — the strongest refusal we have.

**Why it is denied:** `windowsTargetTokens` swallows the abbreviated `-s` value and treats the
following token as a target. Its docstring excused the cost on the grounds that "an unbound
`-Path` fails mandatory binding" — which is **false for this command**, because `-Path` is
bound **by name** in the same line. Citations, verified against the rendered page:
`Remove-Item.md` §`-Path` gives `Required: True, Position: 0`; the FileSystem parameter set is
`Remove-Item [-Path] <String[]> … [-Stream <String[]>]`; §Example 7 runs this exact shape.

**The options:**

1. **Leave it.** The standing rule on this plan is that ambiguity resolves toward firing, and
   a false deny costs a user one prompt while a false allow costs more. The docstring is now
   honest about the cost, which was the actual defect.
2. **Narrow the guard when `-Path` or `-LiteralPath` is explicitly bound.** Sound under both
   readings of the binder — no positional slot is left for the swallowed token — but it
   reverses part of P2.85's decision, and P2.85 exists because a safety here was accidental
   once already.

**Controller recommendation: option 1 for now, and the row is not blocking.** The status quo
is the safe direction, the misleading docstring is already fixed, and the cost is a prompt on
an uncommon command shape. Option 2 is worth taking only if the shape turns out to be common
in practice — which nobody has measured, and which would be the thing to measure first.


## OQ-10 — OPEN: a remote import reads the SERVER OPERATOR's home, not the user's

Surfaced by P2.282 while classifying the two import channels, and rated **low severity on
purpose** by the lane that found it — the reasoning is sound and worth preserving rather than
re-escalating.

**Measured:** for a remote workspace, `workspace:importClaude*` reads the **server operator's**
`~/.claude`, not the requesting user's — against onboarding copy that says *"your Claude Code
setup"*. MCP definitions there can carry credentials in `env`.

**Why the lane rated it low, and I agree:** the same authenticated client can already send a
message to a shell-capable agent on that host. So this is not privilege escalation — it is a
**correctness and expectations** defect: the user is shown someone else's configuration and
told it is theirs.

**Why `LOCAL_ONLY` is not the answer:** it would not fix the confusion, it would **break the
feature** for every remote workspace.

**The options are product ones, which is why this is an OQ rather than a row:**

1. **Say whose setup it is.** Change the copy to name the host, and show the path being read.
   Cheapest, honest, keeps the feature.
2. **Refuse the import on a remote workspace**, with a message explaining why. Safest for the
   credential-exposure reading, and removes a working feature from remote users.
3. **Read the requesting user's home** where the transport can supply it. Correct, and the
   largest piece of work — the client would have to ship the setup rather than the server
   reading it.

**Controller recommendation: option 1 now, option 3 if remote workspaces become common.**
Not blocking; nothing else waits on it.


## OQ-11 — OPEN: "sandbox off" changes nothing, and the agent's shell has no network

Measured by P2.323's lane, live, on the shipped configuration. **No production code was
changed** — the two defensible answers are product decisions.

**What was measured, on all nine probes:** the `danger-full-access` and default configurations
are **behaviourally identical**. `resolveRuntimePolicy` maps `danger-full-access` to profile
parent `:workspace`, the profile always ships, and the profile governs.

**The headline is the network, not writes.** The agent's shell has **no network at all in any
shipped configuration** — and the failure presents as **exit 0 with empty output**, so a model
reads it as *"no such host"* rather than *"you are not allowed"*. That is worse than a refusal:
the agent will conclude the resource does not exist and act on that.

**One option is closed by measurement rather than by taste:** `:danger-full-access` is listed
as a built-in but **cannot be extended** on this pin, so "keep the credential deny, drop the
confinement" is **not expressible by re-parenting**. Anyone reaching for that answer will find
it unavailable.

**The options:**

1. **Make the switch honest** — `danger-full-access` stops shipping a profile, so turning
   isolation off actually turns it off. Matches the affordance's copy and the user's
   expectation. Cost: the credential deny goes with it, and that deny is currently the one
   thing standing between a model and `credentials.enc`.
2. **Keep the confinement and fix the copy** — the switch stays as-is, the UI stops claiming
   it disables isolation, and `runtime-capability-gaps.md` records that codex cannot express
   an unsandboxed session. Cheapest, honest, and it leaves a documented affordance not doing
   what its name says.
3. **Give the network its own answer.** Independent of 1 and 2, the DNS-as-exit-0 shape should
   change: a denied network call should look denied. This is arguably not optional whichever
   of 1 or 2 is chosen, because a model that believes a host does not exist will not retry,
   ask, or report — it will silently work around a restriction nobody told it about.

**Controller recommendation: option 2 plus option 3.** Option 1 trades a working credential
protection for an affordance almost nobody sets deliberately, and P2.306 has already shown how
easily that protection can be removed by accident. Not blocking; P2.331 corrects the copy
either way.


## OQ-12 — OPEN: seven quotation-derived rows are inside the register's 363

Found by P2.339's lane after it fixed the one cell that started this: **the defect was not
exhausted.** Seven further rows in the committed total of 363 are harvested from **quotations**,
all from the two `2026-08-02-claude-doc-sweep-*` survey specs, each adjudicated by reading its
surrounding context (register lines 558, 559, 560, 563, 571 and others).

**The lane deliberately did not suppress them, and the reasoning is sound:** cutting the
headline number by seven on the strength of its own reading risks **dropping a real record**,
which is the worse failure of the two. So they are now **named on every run** rather than
silently included or silently removed.

**Why no parser change can settle it:** the same lane measured that a record's *shape* cannot
distinguish it from a citation. Genuine records live in prose (89), table cells (54), bullets
(215) and at least one blockquote; and 241 of 370 candidates are delimiter-wrapped and nearly
all genuine. **Any rule tight enough to exclude the seven excludes dozens of real ones.**

**The options:**

1. **Adjudicate and suppress** — read each of the seven in context, mark them, and the register
   reads **~356**. Correct, and it costs a careful hour on someone who is willing to be wrong in
   public if a real record is dropped.
2. **Accept documented inflation** — leave 363, with the warning naming the seven on every run.
   Cheapest, honest, and the number stays 2% high forever.

**Controller recommendation: option 1, but not now.** The register is read at close-out, and a
number known to be wrong by seven is a poor thing to close on — but it is also not blocking any
row, and doing it while eight lanes commit means re-adjudicating drift. Take it in the
close-out pass, when the tree is quiet, together with the regeneration P2.340 already owes.


## OQ-13 — OPEN: an unrecognised value for the packaged flag reads as NOT packaged

Recorded by P2.346's lane as a deliberate, documented, test-pinned choice rather than an
accident — which is why it is an open question and not a defect.

**The behaviour:** a value the parser does not recognise (`treu`, an empty string, a stray
quote) reads as **not packaged**, which **re-opens the same fail-open the row just closed** —
the guards go quiet again, for that build.

**Why the lane chose it:** consistency with the four sibling readers, all of which behave that
way. Changing one reader to fail closed while three others fail open would produce a system
that disagrees with itself about what "packaged" means — and disagreement between readers is
precisely what caused the original defect.

**The counter-argument:** this plan's standing direction is that ambiguity resolves toward
firing, and this is a **security guard**. A build whose packaged-ness cannot be determined is
exactly the build that should be treated as packaged, because the guards are cheap and their
absence is what let a bare `'uv'` reach PATH resolution.

**The options:**

1. **Leave it, and consolidate first** (P2.349). Once there is one parse instead of four, the
   fail-closed change is a single edit that cannot desynchronise the readers. **Recommended.**
2. **Flip it now** — a one-line reversal, already identified. Closes the latent hole sooner, at
   the cost of five readers temporarily disagreeing.

Not blocking. Note the practical caveat either way: **the fix does not reach a running app
until `bun run electron:build:servers` restages the two subprocess bundles**, which still carry
the broken comparison — so anyone verifying in `electron:dev` or a packaged build measures the
old code until then.

Two open rows carry the `[remote]` tag: **P2.335** (⏸) and **P2.58** (⬜). *(Corrected 2026-09-02, A2 §3a: measured, `P2.58` carried NO tag and `P3.184` — a codex OS-deny row — carried `[remote]` wrongly; both fixed in the tracker. Resolving (b) by tag would have moved the wrong row.)*

## The row count is not a measure (owner, 2026-08-28)

A milestone of 500 rows was proposed and then **withdrawn by the owner**, for the right reason:
**the plan will keep growing as the runtimes get covered and the host gets written.** New rows
are the work arriving, not the work escaping.

The measurements support that. Row generation is **diffuse, not concentrated** — 187
parent-citations across **93 distinct parents**, about two children each, with no hotspot. And
**40% of all rows were found by a lane fixing something else**, which is a property of the
method rather than of any subsystem. There is no bad area to drain.

But generation **is** decaying by generation, which is what makes an end plausible:

| generation | rows | cited as parent | children per row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P2.1–100 | 100 | 100 | **1.00** |
| P2.101–200 | 100 | 23 | 0.23 |
| P2.201–300 | 100 | 25 | 0.25 |
| P2.301–400 | 53 | 3 | **0.06** |

Sixteenfold down. The early rows were the cost of entering unfamiliar code; the recent ones are
refinements of refinements and barely branch.

**So the measure is not the tracker.** It is:

1. **Coverage of the governing corpus** — the owner's stopping rule, recorded above.
2. **`2026-08-28-capability-ledger.md`** — one row per capability a user can DO or RELY ON,
   three runtime columns, each cell carrying its provenance. Being built now. Pages are not
   capabilities: a page covers several and a capability spans pages, so "N pages green" never
   translated into "the user can do X". That translation is the artifact the plan is measured by.

Closing on an empty tracker was never possible and is no longer the target.


## Priority from 2026-08-28: integration first, defect repair at verification

Owner ruling. The plan continues with its **focus on integrating the available surfaces** of
the claude and codex agent systems, of Pi built to Claude's contract, and of the host that
switches between them. **Defects and residues are recorded as they are found, as before, but
repaired in the verification pass at the end** rather than taken as they arrive.

The reasoning is the owner's and the measurements support it: **most of what this plan finds is
discovered by a lane doing something else** (40% of all rows), so the finding rate falls as the
integration work itself settles rather than as defects are individually chased.

**What this changes in practice**

- Rows tagged `[doc:claude]` / `[doc:codex]` — a contract we should honour — are the queue.
- Rows tagged `[doc:none]` are recorded and **wait for the verification pass**, unless one of
  the two exceptions below applies.
- The capability ledger, not the row count, says what is left.

**Two exceptions, and they are narrow.** A defect is taken immediately if it is (a) a
**shipped security or permission boundary that is currently wrong** — because deferring one of
those means shipping it for longer, and this plan has already found a deny that did not deny, a
guard that never ran and a fix that auto-approved; or (b) **blocking a lane's ability to
measure**, since a broken gate makes every later claim weaker. Everything else waits.

## The verification pass (owner, 2026-08-28)

When the integration work is done, **everything is walked and checked live through CDP, and
walked again per feature and per surface for each runtime**, to confirm nothing was missed or
built wrong.

**The capability ledger is that pass's index.** Every one of its 106 rows resolves to one of
three states, and the third is a real answer rather than a gap:

1. **A live case** — the capability is observable in a running app, so it gets a CDP row.
2. **A latent pin** — real but not live-observable, so a test pins it and the ledger says which.
   A green live pass on a latent capability would certify nothing, which is why
   `testing/parity-wave-verification-checklist.md` already separates 🖐 live from 🧪 latent.
3. **Explicitly out of scope**, with its reason from the four `runtime-capability-gaps.md`
   defines.

**Three things this pass must not inherit**, all measured on this plan:

- **A ledger cell is a claim until the pass confirms it.** 16% of filled cells are propagated
  rather than measured, and a falsifier demoted 11 of 24 it audited — including one refuted by a
  committed measurement sitting in the ledger's own directory.
- **A dev build is not the shipped artefact.** `electron:dev` runs the main process and the Pi
  subprocess from **built bundles**, and two of them currently compile a fixed-then-unrebuilt
  comparison. `bun run electron:build` and `electron:build:servers` are owed **before** any
  session, and live evidence comes from a packaged build.
- **A corrected bundled skill never reaches an existing profile** (`ensureBundledSkills` seeds
  once by slug), so a case exercising one **passes on a fresh profile and fails on the
  operator's real one**. That is not a flake; it is the product, and the pass has to know which
  profile it is measuring.

Per-runtime is the axis that matters here rather than per-page: the same capability can be live
on one runtime, latent on another and structurally absent on a third, and only the runtime cut
shows that.

## Owner decisions 2026-09-05, part 2: the seventeen sitting decisions

The owner read `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-owner-sitting.md` and answered all seventeen
(§1.1–§4.1) in one sitting on 2026-09-05.

**The principle, in the owner's own words:** «делай по рекомендации, чтобы было максимально проще по
интеграции, меньше кода если это возможно, так как рантаймы мы будем часто обновлять. Исключения:
1.1 — нет, мы оставляем пока что выключенный сендбокс / оставляем wildcard. 3.3, 3.4 — обновим все
SDK в конце, ну или по возможности, чтобы выполнить план и уже потом обновить, чтобы проще было
увидеть разницу и покрыть.»

**In English, and it is a STANDING RULE of this plan rather than a one-off answer to these
seventeen:** take the controller recommendation; make the integration as simple as possible and
write as little code as possible where the choice allows it, **because the runtimes will be upgraded
often**. Every line of host code that duplicates or wraps a runtime mechanism is a line that must be
re-measured at each lift, so the least-code answer is the cheapest one to keep true. Where two
options are otherwise close this rule breaks the tie for the smaller one. It does **not** license
removing an honest surface to save code — a disclosure is not the code being economised.

**So every section is decided as its own `*Controller recommendation:*` line states, with the two
exceptions the owner named** — §1.1 (recommendation refused, status quo kept) and §3.3 + §3.4
(recommendation taken, and the lift explicitly moved to the plan's close-out).

### §1.1 The macOS seatbelt wrapper emits `(allow default)` — **EXCEPTION: the recommendation is NOT taken**

**(B) Keep the wildcard**, against the recommended (A). The sandbox stays off by default, the
`(allow default)` profile stays, there is no flip to strict and therefore no `pbpaste` carve-out to
buy. The standing sandbox-off decision of 2026-08-12/13 is reaffirmed a third time, and
`SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD = true` is from today an owner decision of 2026-09-05 rather than a
leftover from a testing period.

**Row P3.330 → ✅, closed: status quo confirmed, and option B's disclosure half is NOT owed.**
Verified at HEAD before closing rather than assumed: the once-per-session success-path warning
(`bash-seatbelt.ts:256` and `:293`, quoting the profile), the real tripwire that replaced the
vacuous guard (`__tests__/bash-seatbelt.test.ts` asserts the RELATION between the constant and the
applied profile in both states, and the strict containment cases now execute today), and the
corrected `sandbox-settings.ts` docblock all landed under `216da994a`. Nothing remains to build, so
the row closes instead of standing open on a debt that is already paid.

### §1.2 A user-scope `env` block is declared, loudly rejected, and never applied

**(A) Refuse permanently**, and disclose the divergence from the documented behaviour rather than
leaving a schema key that reads as supported. Option B's name allowlist would be the ONLY
containment left — the OS-sandbox route is foreclosed by the same 2026-08-12/13 decision — and it is
a list somebody must keep correct forever against a threat model whose worst item is `PATH`. Least
code and least risk agree here.

**Row P3.373 ⏸ → ⬜.** Work follows: the disclosure, plus LOCAL scope's missing refusal record,
which under (A) is a plain defect rather than a design question. The restored pin already landed;
the CA-ladder rung the row worried about becomes moot, because a block that is never applied cannot
outrank `tlsCaPath`. Downstream ⬜ rows citing §1.2 — P6.167, P6.359, P6.491 — are unchanged and now
read a settled answer at their site.

### §1.3 Every runtime hands its whole tool array to whichever model the session points at

**(B) Leave it to its own plan after close-out.** The disclosure notice that makes today's state
honest is built and wired, which was the urgent half. The build half still carries an unsettled
design collision (a restricted host versus the BYO card's default endpoint) and a live-network probe
series that cannot run offline — neither belongs inside this plan.

**Row P3.363 — closed, status quo confirmed (stays ✅).** Its own plan runs after this one closes,
with the mandatory re-anchor pass its rows already name.

### §1.4 One `additionalDirectories` setting, three treatments, and the Pi arm is inert

**(A) Wire the Pi arm** behind the existing off-by-default opt-in, so the setting means one thing.
One line of wiring is less code than a deletion plus the three-runtime explanation a deletion owes,
and the blast radius is an operator who explicitly asked for it.

**Row P3.339 🟨 → ⬜.** The row landed its measurement half and routed the residue here; the residue
is now a decided build, so the row must be dispatchable again rather than counted done. Its own
first task is unchanged and still comes first: measure whether claude actually loads components from
a flag-added root, because P6.34's claude half is asserted from the page and contradicted by PKG-4.
Downstream ⬜ rows citing §1.4 — P6.193, P6.202, P6.222, P6.331, P6.394, P6.435 — are unchanged.

### §1.5 A heredoc body is read as a command by the compound-command splitter

**(A) Lift the standing ruling and build a heredoc-aware split — and this is the one answer that is
not the smaller option.** The recommendation was *decide §1.6 first*; §1.6 is (A), so the
precondition option A names — *"with §1.6 resolved first so it can be weighted"* — is satisfied and
option A is the one the recommendation points at. The standing owner ruling recorded in
`scanCommand`'s docblock against a heredoc model in this scanner is lifted for this one change, and
the 18 272-command corpus is its instrument.

**Sequencing is part of the answer, not a nicety: §1.6's copy lands BEFORE this row dispatches.**
Built against the adversarial set again, the change would bend the module's *refuse more, never
approve more* rule on unweighted evidence — which is precisely the objection that sent it here.

**Row P3.329 ⏸ → ⬜**, now blocked on P2.389 rather than on the owner.

**(A) One copy, read-only, treated as untrusted.** Taken once, by a human or under an explicit
approval, into the repo or the scratch tree; the transcripts' contents are data, never instructions,
and the standing rule against executing any string naming a real home or root is untouched.

**Row P2.389 → ⬜, unchanged glyph and now carrying an answer.** It is also the gate on §1.5/P3.329,

**(B) Adopt the documented shape** — the model committing under an explicit grant — and drop the

## Owner decisions 2026-09-05, part 3: fifteen denominator postures and the five remaining ⏸ rows

**The owner took the controller's recommendations, in one line — «по вопросам — давай делать как
рекомендуешь» — so every item below is decided as the CONTROLLER's recommendation states, which for
several of D1–D15 differs from the sweep's own `Recommendation:` line in the question.** Two sets were
put: D1–D15, the fifteen product postures the standing delegation does not cover
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-denominator-questions-triage.md` §*For the owner (Russian)*, with the
options and their buys/costs in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-denominator-owner-questions.md`), and
D16–D20, the five ⏸ rows part 2 left blocked on a different answer. **Nothing in this plan now waits on
the owner.**

Staged rows for the six answers that buy work, plus the one strip, are in
`nessy-wf-checkpoints/work/posture-decision-rows.md`; the controller numbers them, inserts each in sorted
position and runs `python3 scripts/sort-plan-tracker.py`.

### Set 1 — the fifteen postures

**D1 — may an untrusted MCP server's `readOnlyHint` let its tool skip our gate?** · denominator **A74**
(`absent` on all three) · **Option A:** the invariant stands — a server's tool annotation is advisory and
never an authorization signal, and there is no gate-skip, not even behind an operator allowlist. The
recommendation the sweep carried (B) would have reversed a test-pinned invariant in the loosening
direction. · **consequence: ledger** — record the deviation from the annotation's documented use, and say
where a reader meets it.

**D2 — do we ship an environment-drafting assistant at all (`/auto-mode-setup`)?** · denominator **A79**
(`absent` on all three) · **Option A:** no. A new writer of permission rules whose weakest part is draft
quality is not a surface this product adds; the `autoMode` allow block is written by an administrator.
C (reading shell history and home-directory repositories) is refused under every option. ·
**consequence: none** — status quo, and the absence is uniform.

**D3 — a per-session scratch directory whose writes never raise a permission prompt.** · denominator
**A81** (`absent` on all three, size S) · **Option B:** yes — one host-owned job directory per session,
**named in the gate's own diagnostic**, outside the workspace, torn down with the session; on claude it is
the runtime's own `CLAUDE_JOB_DIR` (native-first tier 1, the SDK already reads it) and on Pi and codex a
host-supplied equivalent, which is a switch verdict owed to the gaps doc. The teardown and the
never-re-read-into-context property are each pinned by a test. · **consequence: row.**

**D4 — a runtime-blind multi-session screen.** · denominator **F27** (`absent` on all three, size L) ·
**Option A now:** do not build it in this plan; revisit after close-out. An L build with its own i18n,
playground states and a Phase-4 design pass is a new product surface rather than a parity repair. ·
**consequence: ledger** — the page-level divergence is already recorded
(`2026-08-02-claude-doc-sweep-divergences.md:461`, row 52) and the smallest honest piece is already rowed
as **P6.270**.

**D5 — how does a user's own environment reach a host-run command hook?** · denominator **G15** (pi
`absent`, claude `partial`, codex `absent`) · **Option A:** the six-name whitelist stays, and the
divergence is disclosed. This is the answer that is CONSISTENT with sitting §1.2 = A, decided in part 2 on
the same containment argument — the question says in terms to answer them together, and its own
recommendation (B) inverts under that answer. · **consequence: ledger**, against §1.2's row **P3.373**.

**D6 — per-dimension sandbox escape valves, or one coarse valve?** · denominator **I28** (`absent` on all
three, size M) · **Option B:** project the native container and proxy keys, and **refuse
`allowAppleEvents` permanently, by name** — it removes code-execution isolation on macOS, which is a
safety trade and not a convenience. A is the status quo dressed as a decision and the weaker posture,
because `excludedCommands` deletes the boundary for a command where a dimension key would only widen it.
**Low priority**: the sandbox is off by standing decision, reaffirmed as sitting §1.1, so this is
sequenced and never raced. · **consequence: row — already carried**, by **P6.233** (the container key and
the network-isolation weakener) and **P6.253** (the proxy ports and the Unix-socket keys). **P6.233's
`done_means` is AMENDED**: it currently says `allowAppleEvents` should be parsed and projected, and this
decision refuses it by name, with the refusal visible to an operator and stated in the gaps doc.

**D7 — is containerised execution a direction for this product at all?** · denominator **I31** (`absent`
on all three) · **Option c:** not now — record the uniform absence. Option b (claude's own
`spawnClaudeCodeProcess` hook, leaving Pi and codex outside) is refused under every reading, because it
would manufacture exactly the silent divergence native-first exists to prevent. · **consequence: ledger.**

**D8 — Windows: the weaker `unelevated` sandbox, or provisioning codex's `elevated`?** · denominator
**I32** (Pi `absent`, claude `n/a`, codex `unknown`) · **Option A:** keep `unelevated` and record it
honestly. Provisioning creates local sandbox users and a secrets store on the user's machine — a first-run
experience and an operator cost — and it cannot be costed without the Windows rig **P3.7** is parked for.
P3.7 stays parked. · **consequence: ledger**, and the codex `[windows]`-block measurement owed under every
option is already **P6.227**.

**D9 — governing the built-in browser: per-site approval and the CDP grant.** · denominator **J12** (pi
`partial`, claude `partial`, codex `absent`, size L) and **J14** (pi `absent`, claude `absent`, codex
`n/a`, size M) · **Option 2:** a host per-origin trust store — Allow once / Always allow / Deny, per
subdomain, revocable — gating **both** the first navigation to a new origin **and** the first full-CDP
attach on that origin, plus a managed lock beside `disableInAppBrowser`. Option 3 (a classifier band over
external-origin write actions, and a browsing-session persistence choice) is the destination and comes
later, never before the card exists. Option 1 is the one option in this group that is **not honest** —
nothing today tells the user or the operator that browsing is ungoverned. The accepted cost is named: Pi
and claude users will meet approvals they have never seen, because today's gate is per-COMMAND. ·
**consequence: row**, sequenced behind **P6.338** (denominator J15, the operator half, which needs no
owner input and whose allowlist this card consumes).

**D10 — background distillation of finished chats into durable memories.** · denominator **L49** (pi
`partial`, claude `unknown`, codex `absent`, size L) · **Option 1 now:** memory stays invoke-only on all
three. A host distiller is refused outright — it buys a background model call per finished chat, the same
invisible recurring spend the session-summary question refused an hour earlier, and writes durable
memories from conversations with no model in the loop. If distillation is ever wanted it arrives
**codex-native with disclosure**, never as a host distiller. · **consequence: ledger**, and **P6.166**
(codex's two native auto-memory off keys) stands as the precondition either way.

**D11 — may an operator supply the model price table?** · denominator **M9** (`absent` on all three;
unblocks the `managed` value of **M10**'s basis label) · **Option A:** yes — a host-side managed price
table read by all three runtimes, **operator-supplied and never bundled by us**, with every figure
carrying its basis label so a managed price is visibly a managed price. The cost is named: the operator
maintains the list, and a wrong entry produces a confidently wrong figure and a cap that fires at the
wrong moment — which is why the label is part of done_means rather than a follow-up. ·
**consequence: row**, feeding **P6.445**'s basis label and making **P6.507**'s USD arm real.

**D12 — may the configuration checkup change anything after you confirm?** · denominator **M14**
(`absent` on all three) · **Option A:** it stays **read-only, and says so**. The CLI form already quotes
the line back at itself; a checkup that edits the user's files is a different product. ·
**consequence: ledger**, and one of option B's two finding classes is already rowed as **P6.398**.

**D13 — may host telemetry name a person and a session?** · denominator **M33** (pi `absent`, claude
`absent`, codex `partial`; gates the correlation-id rider on **M31**) · **Option B:** identity behind the
documented toggles, **default off** — the vendors' own switch names on claude and codex, one host
implementation for Pi. Already the recorded recommendation at
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-observability-and-cost.md:183` («the toggles, not a default»). The cost
is named: a real per-user identifier can leave the machine once an administrator enables it, so the user
whose session is named must be told, and Pi's HMAC scheme gains a second, non-anonymous mode. C (content)
is **not** decided here — it is D14. · **consequence: row**, with **P6.460** (M31) riding it.

**D14 — may an ambient shell variable make a session export its whole conversation?** · denominator
**M34** (pi `absent`, claude `have`, codex `absent`) · **Option A:** **strip** the four `OTEL_LOG_*`
content opt-ins from the claude child's environment and keep codex pinned off. This removes a working
vendor capability, deliberately, on the owner's own recorded pattern for a one-runtime capability — and
the status quo is the one thing neither option keeps: today an inherited `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=1`
exports the whole conversation with no host decision anywhere. If content export is wanted later it
arrives as an explicit host setting and never as an inherited variable. · **consequence: row**, sequenced
with **P6.452**'s M21 unit, which edits the same `buildClaudeSubprocessEnv` site.

**D15 — a repository's checked-in `.codex/` layer, and codex's own trust model.** · denominator **L22**
(pi `unknown`, claude `unknown`, codex `absent`, size M) · **Option 2:** project the host's existing
`projectTrusted` onto codex's own `trust_level` — the native-first ordering exactly, since codex's own
trust gate decides and `is_untrusted()` keeps the repo layer out. **The caveat is recorded rather than
discovered later:** a trusted project's checked-in `.codex/` gains real effect, including keys we do not
audit, and codex's own rule at `config_toml.rs:743-747` seeds **`sandbox_mode`** from the same decision,
so a repository gains influence over the sandbox. That consequence is written at the write site and on a
user-reachable surface. The credential floor is unchanged (sitting §3.1). · **consequence: row**,
sequenced after **P6.195** and **P6.196**.

### Set 2 — the five ⏸ rows part 2 left, D16–D20

**D16 — P2.318, the codex model preference list is one-of-seven live.** · **Option B:** it stays parked as
gated until the ChatGPT card is enabled — the list is keyed on `openai-codex`, the flag-off Plus/Pro OAuth
card, and the owner's 2026-08-29 ruling on that surface is *do not build, do not delete, do not clean up*.
**One comment** marking the preference list decorative today is added, and that comment is the row's whole
remaining deliverable. · **consequence: row** — **P2.318 ⏸ → ⬜.**

**D17 — P2.335, the cloud agent has no corpus to check it against.** · **Option A:** a narrow lane on the
cloud agent's **emission discipline** — the one thing the new probe already makes measurable — and the
corpus starts as a **list**, not a document. The owner's 2026-08-29 re-framing stands: `nestor-cloud-agent`
is a remote agent with no local runtime, so it is not a fourth ledger column; the re-check the owner asked
for folds into **P5.4**. · **consequence: row** — **P2.335 ⏸ → ⬜.**

**D18 — P2.357, a dead reset feature is the only thing keeping 34 setters harmless.** · **Option A:**
record the dependency **at both ends now** — in `clearAllConfig`'s docstring and in the setters' shared
comment — so a future author wiring a reset or logout meets the consequence in the file rather than in a
plan. Whether warn-and-return-false is adequate once the state is reachable is revisited **if** such a
feature is built, not now. · **consequence: row** — **P2.357 ⏸ → ⬜.**

**D19 — P3.90, the gateway returns 500 on a wrong credential type.** · **Option A:** our own models
fetcher treats a 5xx on the models endpoint as **non-retryable-with-a-diagnosis** rather than a transient,
so a user who pastes the wrong key is told "wrong credential" instead of waiting out a backoff. The
upstream report to the gateway team, with the request id, is the **owner's** to make and is not this
plan's work. · **consequence: row** — **P3.90 ⏸ → ⬜.**

**D20 — P6.9, the corporate-launcher seam.** · **Confirmed OUT of this plan**: the owner's 2026-08-28
deferral stands — *«этого не будет, я бы не стал сейчас это делать»*, *«я бы сместил это аж в самую
последнюю очередь»*. The measurement stands and is not refuted (three live unwrapped spawn sites, UNIFORM
across all three runtimes, `absent` everywhere); the seam changes how an organisation OBSERVES the agent,
not what the agent can do, and the four goals are about the agent loop. Ledger **C4** stays
`absent — DECISION`. · **consequence: parked** (closed out of scope, not built) — **P6.9 ⏸ → ✅.**

## Controller decisions 2026-09-05 (delegated) — findings born in wave 6

Under the owner's 2026-09-05 delegation (decide in line with the goal, put it in the plan, no question unless the
product's posture changes), the controller ruled on the lane findings as they were confirmed:

- **PN-1 (W6-b, P6.74)** — `channelsEnabled` / `allowedChannelServers` fit none of the managed-key scale's poles. Ruling:
  NO fifth state; the keys stay `unmeasured` with the finding as the reason. A fifth state changes the admin surface for
  two keys nobody has set. Consequence: `ledger`.
- **PN-2 → P6.541**, **PN-3 → P6.542**, **PN-4 → P6.543**, **PN-5 → P6.544** (W6-b). PN-3 is decided in the parity
  direction (both runtimes) because the measured alternative broke a no-degradation control.
- **W6-c proposed rows 1–3 → P6.545, P6.546, P6.547.** P6.547 takes the documented shape narrowly: delete only a clean,
  host-created branch (`git branch -d`), never force.
- **W6-c deviation accepted:** P6.136 landed before P6.135 (the killed instance had already built it; disjoint regions,
  suites re-run after both).
- **W7-b lane-level finding (2026-09-05):** six of its nine rows have their deliverable in a file the lane may not write —
  the wave-7 zones were derived from where each fact was MEASURED, not where the fix lands. Ruling: the write-set of a lane
  is the union of the citation seam and the file that already writes the surface named in `done_means`; the six rows are
  re-zoned by name (`nessy-wf-checkpoints/work/rezone.md`, mirrored in each row's note) and travel with the later lanes'
  briefs. W7-b's proposed row (2) (E11 has no ledger row) is P6.189's; (4) is P6.549; (5)/(6) — `lint:conditional-expect`
  and `typecheck:electron` red on other lanes' uncommitted files — are transient and fall to the wave gate.
- **W7-g lane-level finding (2026-09-06), the same defect a second time:** seven of ten rows re-zoned — the deliverables'
  call sites are `SessionManager.ts` (five) and the agent files, which have no W7-G1 holder. Ruling: wave 8 and every later
  brief zone by the `done_means` WRITE SET; W7-G1 lanes finish as measuring lanes and their re-zoned rows travel with W7-l,
  W7-s, W7-m, W7-r, W7-i (`nessy-wf-checkpoints/work/rezone.md`). Also recorded there: the pi-agent-server `check:surface --pin`
  rule (commit only your own digest lines of `tool-surface.json`).
- **W6-d process finding (2026-09-06):** a bare `git add` + `git commit` in the shared tree committed ANOTHER lane's staged
  index (P6.69's diff landed inside `3a7677b54`, a wave-7 i18n commit whose message says "committed alone"; nothing lost, the
  row→sha mapping was). Wave rule: only the atomic `git commit -F <msg> -- <pathspec>`. Recorded in AGENTS.md §Traps.

(5) **The strength question is ANSWERED by the module's own revealed standard, so this row no longer needs a model experiment to start:** the seam already defangs `\t  User:` and lowercase `user:` — neither byte-identical to a host entry — while the NBSP deferral dismissed NBSP *because* it is not byte-identical. By its own standard, NBSP is in. **CLOSED in one commit — and BOTH ROWS WERE WRONG ABOUT THE FIX SITE.** `wrapUntrusted` does not defang; it delegates to `neutralizeHarnessMarkers`, and **ten other sites call that with no fence anywhere near them** (advisor context and question, side question, transfer banner, guardian org-policy and judge reason, the prompt-builder's server/plugin/label names, task-notification). Fixed one layer down instead: measured **0/36 → 36/36** across all three entrances. **And the obvious fix OPENS A HOLE — this is the finding to carry forward.** Renderers defang openers per entry and *then* fence the join, so a strip placed at the fence alone runs AFTER the per-entry defang and **reassembles what the defang had broken**: `Us`+U+0001+`er:` is inert today and becomes a **live forged `User:`** with the strip in the fence only. The strip therefore has to sit at **two** entrances, and mutant M3 reproduces the reassembly exactly. **Eight escapes, not six** — U+200B and U+00AD were on neither list, U+202E is the same class. Evidence: transcript-fences **63 pass / 0 fail**, the affected 10-file batch 145/1 skip/0, Pi child-output neutraliser 12/0/0, direct callers 208/0/0, typecheck shared + server-core clean, **5 mutants killed**, and an over-fire delta of **+0** across 5,354 files / 2,145,368 lines. | P2.99 | the word-start set is Unicode-wide, not the shell blank set | ✅ | 103287d76+fedd86c67 | Found by the P2.71/P2.75 chain re-review (F1 Critical + F2 Critical), controller-confirmed on its own matcher AND real shell. Where unsure, err toward FEWER recognized comments (fewer excisions on sh, fewer suppressions on PS — the safe direction for both, since excision-unsafe and suppression-unsafe both point at recognizing TOO MANY comments). Fold in F3: three docstrings assert the exact property this violates — `claude-bash-rule.ts:114` "strict SUBSET of the shells … we scan MORE rather than less", `:186` "this pass cannot hide from a deny rule text the shell would execute", and the PS twin "we scan more, never less" (d76df0fbf) — correct all three to the true post-fix property. BUT keeping `\r` in the sh predicate is itself a Critical: POSIX sh does NOT treat a bare CR as a line terminator (measured `echo a\recho B` runs as ONE command), so `<word>\r#x ; rm -rf ~` opens a comment the shell never opens and the `;` still runs the tail — DSL `deny Bash(rm:*)`→undefined, breaker→null, `__PWNED__` printed; 8 under-fire holes across `;`/` **CLOSED (103287d76 word-boundary + fedd86c67 CR), chain-reviewer fuzz + CONTROLLER re-confirmation on HEAD.** The re-review agent hit the session limit mid-run but had already produced the decisive measurement: full 9,906-probe differential fuzz on the CR-fix HEAD = **2 holes, both the pre-existing ANSI-C glued-head artifact (byte-identical on the parent); zero Unicode (F1), zero CR, zero BOM (F2)**. Controller re-confirmed all four on HEAD with its own matcher rig: F1 `git status\u00a0# ok ; rm -rf ~` deny→match + breaker→home; CR `echo a\r#x <sep> rm -rf ~` deny→match on `;`/`\|`/`&&`/`&`; F2 `gci\uFEFF# note ; Remove-Item /` allow→no-match (widen closed); CRLF over-fire settled as SAFE — `cat file\r\n# rm -rf ~` splits to `['cat file','# rm -rf ~']` (deny no-match, matching the shell which treats the line-start `#` as a comment and runs no rm), and the under-fire control `cat file\r\nrm -rf ~` (real rm, no `#`) still deny→match. The 2 ANSI-C survivors are pre-existing (byte-identical on parent), tracked as P2.104. \|`/`&&`/`&`. The implementer's own inline comment at `claude-bash-rule.ts:301` says CR "leave[s] `a<WS>#` one word and run[s] the tail" then the next line keeps `\r` — self-contradiction. **Fix: drop `\r` → `[ \t\n]`** (closes all 8, keeps LF/SP/P2.71 excision, only over-fires CRLF-line-start comments = safe; no shipped test uses bare-CR-before-#, so tests stay green). | P2.113 | sed's `e` execution primitive is on an axis letter-absence cannot close | ✅ | 42ebdc062 | Reported by P2.6's fix wave 3 rather than silently shipped, and it is the honest residue of that wave's design. Sits beside P2.109/P2.112 as the isolation-scanner residue set. **RE-GRADED: LIVE on shipped Linux builds, not theoretical.** Measured by P2.6's wave-3 re-review: both forms are allowed by the gate (`sed -n 'e touch x' f` and `sed -n 's/.*/touch x/e' f` — note an attacker uses a `w`-free payload precisely so the letter-absence scanner does not catch it incidentally). macOS/BSD sed rejects it (`sed: 1: "e touch pwned": invalid command code e`), so the deferral reasoning was right about BSD — **but `apps/electron/scripts/` ships `build-linux.sh` alongside build-dmg.sh and build-win.ps1, and Linux is GNU sed, where `e` EXECUTES.** So this is a live execution primitive on a ship target, and its priority should reflect that rather than the macOS measurement. A conservative sed walk now decides, and **every uncertainty falls back to the letter test, so a misparse costs an over-block and never a bypass** — the failure direction chosen deliberately. Hooked into **both** paths, gated on the sed head. Platform note measured rather than assumed: BSD sed **rejects** `e` (positive control on the same rig: `w` did write), while `build-linux.sh` ships where **GNU sed executes it** — so the exposure is real on the platform we ship to, not on the one we test on. **[guard, shared across this lane's six rows] Self-test 65/65 — and its FIRST DRAFT HAD A HOLE that a live negative control caught: `touch /private/tmp/…` was permitted and REALLY CREATED THE FILE.** That is the same "absent from a negative list" defect these rows fix in the product, reproduced inside the safety harness itself. | P2.136 | a managed lock is sent without its operand, inverting the admin's intent | ✅ | 5d812230b | Found by P2.7's review (M-2) and it is the ONE silent drop in that commit. Measured on HEAD: a policy carrying `sandbox{ network{allowManagedDomainsOnly:true, allowedDomains:['corp.example']}, filesystem{allowManagedReadPathsOnly:true, allowRead:['/opt/corp']} }` reaches the SDK as the LOCKS WITHOUT THEIR LISTS — and the SDK's own strings describe `allowManagedDomainsOnly` as \"deterministically denies hosts not in `allowedDomains`\", so a lock with an empty managed list is **deny-every-host and deny-every-read**. The admin wrote an allowlist and got a deny-all. Fail-closed, so not a security hole — but it INVERTS intent, and the surfacing says nothing: `mapped=['sandbox']`, `unsupported=[]`, diagnostics \"carries: sandbox\". Root cause is a category error the mapper makes: `allowedDomains`/`allowRead` are treated as WIDENINGS and withheld, when riding with their `allowManaged*Only` lock they are the lock's OPERAND — and `Ebg` would have carried them (`t.sandbox?.network?.allowManagedDomainsOnly!==!0 && o.allowedDomains`, where `t` is composed from admin tiers only, never from our slice). Fix: send the list whenever its lock is set, and make the surfacing report at SUB-KEY granularity so a withheld operand cannot read as a wholly-mapped key. **CLOSED — operand carry AND sub-key surfacing both landed, and the feared consumer blocker did not exist:** the finer shape is purely additive (`withheld` is a NEW field; `mapped`/`unsupported` keep their whole-key meaning), and the only production consumer repo-wide is `packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts` symbol `claudeManagedSettings`, which reads just `.settings` and the formatted lines. **Two corrections to this row's own text, neither changing the fix.** First, the quoted sentence "deterministically denies hosts not in `allowedDomains`" is **`strictAllowlist`'s** string, not `allowManagedDomainsOnly`'s — the deny-every-host conclusion still holds, but through that key's own sentence ("blocks a non-allowed domain automatically instead of prompting"), so the row was right for a slightly wrong reason. Second, **"deny-every-read" overstates the filesystem half**: `allowRead` re-opens paths *inside* `denyRead` regions rather than gating reads outright, so a lock without its list means "nothing is re-opened" — which in this row's own fixture, carrying no `denyRead`, is close to **inert**. Evidence: **37 pass / 0 fail** (11 added, and **1 corrected test that had been pinning the defect**), re-breaking the operand carry alone fails 6, typecheck/eslint/diff-check clean. Residue → P2.267, P2.268. |

`list_agents.rs`/`send_message.rs` exist **only** under `multi_agents_v2/`, pinned `enabled FALSE, defaultEnabled false` at `config-writer-operator-ceilings.test.ts:60-73`, and those agents are codex-spawned collaborators in one process, not the host's other sessions — **native-first answers do-not-adopt**, since enabling v2 would put a second, differently-scoped `send_message`/`list_agents` in front of the model. **Tier 2 (the host already has it, reuse rather than rebuild):** the expiring approve/deny card exists — `AskUserRequest.tsx:26-51` `useAskUserAutoContinue(timeoutMs, onExpire)`, `timeoutMs === undefined` arms nothing (which *is* `dialogExpiry: 'never'`) and `onExpire` fires exactly once at the deadline, beside `PermissionRequest.tsx` / `AdminApprovalRequest.tsx` / `CredentialRequest.tsx` in the same directory; the decision input is host-uniform too (`managed.permissionMode`, `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts` symbol `permissionMode`; the seven values in `PiHarnessPermissionModeV1`, `packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:9`). **`done_means`** — with no `NESSY_CROSS_SESSION_INBOUND` and no settings value: (a) bypass sender → prompting receiver raises an approval card; (b) **prompting sender → bypassing receiver ALSO holds** (the arm that fires for every `bypassPermissions` desktop session); (c) Approve delivers that one message, Deny or dismiss drops it; (d) unanswered past `dialogExpiry` drops it and reports `expired` to the sender, `'never'` honoured; (e) while no client is attached the deadline is suspended and restarts on attach; (f) a permission-mode change re-applies and releases; (g) a refuse arriving while held drops all and reports a refusal; (h) session end reports every still-held message as expired to each reachable sender; (i) a `/config` row writes the value to user settings, is hidden while managed settings or `--settings` set the key, and rejects the `crossSessionInbound=value` shorthand. Then the identical observable is driven on a **claude-runtime** session (N2-claude) and on a **codex** session (N2-codex) — the latter only after asserting `getSchedulingBridgeState() === 'active'` (`packages/shared/src/agent/codex-agent.ts` symbol `getSchedulingBridgeState`), because an unbridged codex session never binds `sendAgentMessage` at all (`session-mcp-server/src/index.ts:196` opens the conditional spread, `:205` `sendAgentMessage: createBridgeSendAgentMessage(bridge)` sits inside it) and a rig that skipped the check would read "no message arrived" as "the gate held it". A **divergence** between the three is the failure — it would mean the gate acquired a runtime branch. **ORDERING CONSTRAINT: the mode-derived default and the card must land in ONE change** — the default alone turns today's documented `accept` (`cross-session-inbound.ts:82-84`, "Until that lands, no value means `accept`") into a silent drop, the exact SILENT-LOOSER shape this ledger exists to catch. **Evidence:** `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging.md#control-inbound-messages` (fetched 200, 365 lines) — line 221 "**The receiving session prompts for permissions**: Claude Code delivers each message. It holds one for your approval only when the sending session identifies itself as bypassing permission prompts", line 222 "**The receiving session bypasses permission prompts**: Claude Code holds each message for your approval. It delivers one only when the sending session identifies itself as also bypassing.", line 228 the detached arm, line 247 the session-end expiry report, line 217 the `/config` row's three constraints; `dialogExpiry` appears in this tree exactly once, as prose at `cross-session-inbound.ts:81` (`git grep -an dialogExpiry -- packages apps` → 1 hit). Closed rows read: P6.45/P6.46 (`fd0388b05`, plan lines 3603-3604 — "a session cannot refuse or hold an inbound message from another session"), P2.460 (`3f5767406`), P3.222 (`c197a8bb4`, `cfe66e51e`). O26 (out-of-scope register line 60) records the key as read by nobody — a record, not a scope-out. **CLOSED 2026-09-08 (W9-l): clauses (a)–(h) LANDED `2b6fdd3f6`** — a session can hold or refuse an inbound message from another session, default + card in one change. Clause (i) (the `/config` row) stays a HELD residue for W9-q (group 7), recorded there. **W9-ar (2026-09-08): clause (i) LANDED `60ef8739c`** — the user rung + the `/config` row + the resolver.
